blocks.text: For members of many Annelida, the epidermis is underlain by layer a of circular muscle (Purschke and Miiller, 2006; Tzetlin and Filippova, 2005). Beneath the circular muscle layer lie thick longitudinal muscles (Fig. 2.1c). The circular muscle layer forms, a nearly continuous sheath around the body, except in those) annelids with well-developed parapodia. Notably, the absence of a circular muscle layer has been reported in wide now a range of annelid taxa: Polygordius, Protodrilidae, Aphroditiformia, Chrysopetatidae, Nephtyidae, Phyllodocidae, Sphaerodoridae, Nerilli- dae, Serpulidae, Spionida, Opheliidae (some), Magelona, and Oweni- idae (Filippova al., Filippova et 2005; et al., 2010; Law et al., Miiller, Riichel and 2014; 2006; Mueller, 2007; Tzetlin and Filip- pova, 2005). This has raised questions as to the plesiomorphic condition for musculature in Polychaeta and also for Anneli- da (Purschke and Miiller, 2006; ‘Tzetlin and Filippova, 2005). While interesting, the absence of circular muscles in Oweniida does not mean this is the plesiomorphic condition for Anneli- da. Circular muscles are present in Chaetopteriformia taxa, such as Apistobranchidae and Psammodrilidae (Orrhage, 1974; Worsaae, 2019), and also in Amphinomida (Purschke and Miiller, 2006) and Sipuncula (Kristof et al., 2011).
